Both arms reserve and use the same two banked 1R1W destination accumulator slots and output sink. external_prior.borrowed_mechanism: Adjacent-position event compression with exact intersection, residual event streams and cached overlap partial sums.

cycle_model.scratch_port: one synchronous 1R1W 128-byte/cycle port, one-cycle response; write and read phases serialize
cycle_model.weight_path: eight lockstep INT8 banks, aggregate 128 bytes/cycle, same mapping and one-cycle startup in both arms
cycle_model.baseline_mode: The exact same APEC-capable top with compression disabled; comparator, pair bitmap, 16.03125-KiB overlap cache, two destination slots, all banks and queue entry remain physically reserved but candidate-only logic is clock-gated.
cycle_model.candidate_mode: Exact horizontal G2. Per group, common events execute once; one overlap vector is written once and synchronously read twice to seed two ordinary banked 1R1W destination accumulators. Residual events use the same destination RMW path as baseline events. Both modes finally read the same two shifted destination vectors into the same sink.
cycle_model.service_equation: For a destination stream with E events and k valid taps: compute=E*ceil(768*k/96); each of eight weight banks serves E*k*96 bytes at 16 B/cycle; each destination bank serves 12 lanes*19 bit/cycle through one 1R1W 32 B/cycle port and pays one synchronous tail per nonempty stream. A non-seeded destination pays a banked zero-write pass. Group bitmap traffic is two cycles in both arms; candidate adds one exact-compare cycle. Final commit pipelines a destination-slot read into the common eight-bank 16 B/cycle sink and pays the slower side. An overlap group adds one scratch write plus two synchronous scratch reads; each scratch response seeds a separately ported destination slot and pays its response tail.
cycle_model.border_rule: Each source position pays only valid 3x3 taps. The common overlap vector uses the union of valid kernel offsets for the adjacent pair. Width 20 has no G2 tail.
cycle_model.queue_and_stall_rule: A conservative serialized group schedule with one ready/valid queue entry is used. Destination zero/seed, RMW, final read, sink write, weight-not-ready, next-group backpressure and candidate-only scratch serialization/tails are reported explicitly. Destination RMW may overlap MAC only after per-bank bandwidth proves the 96-lane demand; final slot read may pipeline only with its sink write. No scratch phase overlaps event service and no free port or second issue queue is assumed.

frozen_envelope.use: Amdahl replacement sensitivity only. The standalone M507 cycle ratio replaces this frozen share analytically and is never called a system simulation.

fail_closed: Abort on any input SHA, manifest schema/status, payload SHA, decoded payload, shape, codebook, event-conservation or M501-ledger mismatch.
Both arms must derive the same 240 KiB capacity ledger and identical ports; no free boolean is accepted as evidence.

Every destination capacity item has named bank, 1R1W, width and synchronous-read semantics. Both arms reserve the same destination slots and pay byte/cycle-conserving zero-or-seed, RMW and final-read/sink-write paths.
Every synchronous overlap-cache read pays its final response tail; serialized phases are reported as stalls/backpressure rather than a constant zero conflict counter.
Never overlap scratch write/read/commit with event service; doing so would add an unproven port or schedule.
Never call the charged envelope sensitivity a measured system cycle speedup.
Never claim APEC, binary support intersection or this positive two-codeword trace as a new signed-analog mechanism.
This is the single authorized fast-kill. No post-hoc vertical/G4/G8 retry is allowed.
